title: One blast of the Horn, and it begins.
subtitle: Allah's command needs no second time
then: Ibn Kathir describes the blowings of the Horn: of fright, of destruction, then {idea}of standing before the Lord of all that exists.{/idea} It is called one blowing because {idea}the command of Allah cannot be opposed{/idea} and does not need repeating.
now: Your alarm rings and you hit snooze three times. Your mother calls you for dinner five times. {trap}We are used to second chances to get up.{/trap} {idea}On that Day, one call is enough for everyone.{/idea}
old: I will respond when the call gets serious.
new: When Allah calls, there is no snooze. Better to answer His calls now.
try: Get up for the next adhan on the first call, without waiting.

title: Earth and mountains lifted and leveled in one blow.
subtitle: The firmest things are not permanent
then: Ibn Kathir says the earth and mountains {trap}will be stretched out to the extent of the surface{/trap}, and {idea}the earth will change into something other than the earth.{/idea} All of it in a single crushing.
now: You say solid as a rock. You buy land because land lasts. Your house sits on ground you never think about. {trap}Even mountains are temporary.{/trap} {idea}Build on what does not end.{/idea}
old: Some things in this world are permanent.
new: Even mountains will be leveled. Only Allah and what is for Him remains.
try: Next time you see a hill or a tall building today, remember it is temporary and say subhanAllah.

title: On that Day, the Event will have happened.
subtitle: The waiting is over
then: After the Horn and the leveling, the verse says the Event {idea}will occur{/idea}, and Ibn Kathir explains it means {idea}the Day of Judgment.{/idea} The deniers of Makkah who said it would never come would see it.
now: You keep saying I will start next month. Next Ramadan. When things calm down. {trap}There will be a day when there is no next.{/trap} {idea}That Day is called the Event.{/idea}
old: There is always more time to get ready.
new: The Event will come as surely as if it already happened.
try: Take one good thing you keep postponing and start a small piece of it today.

title: The sky will split, weak and torn that Day.
subtitle: The roof over the world gives way
then: Ibn Jurayj linked this to another verse: {idea}the heaven shall be opened, it will become as gates.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said {trap}the sky will be torn apart{/trap}, and the Throne will be near it.
now: You look up from the bus stop and the sky is just there, blue or grey, always. {idea}It holds because Allah holds it.{/idea} One day He will let it open.
old: The sky is just the background of my life.
new: The sky stays whole by Allah's command, and one day it will open.
try: Look up at the sky once today for ten seconds and remember Who holds it.

title: Angels at the edges, and eight bear the Throne.
subtitle: The scene of the Lord's court

row.title: the angels
sub: on the sides of the sky

then: Ar-Rabi' said the angels will stand {idea}on the sides of the heavens, looking at the people of the earth.{/idea} Eight angels will carry the Throne. The Prophet ﷺ said of one of them: {idea}between his earlobe and shoulder is seven hundred years of travel.{/idea}
now: You have stood in a big airport, a stadium, a grand hall, and felt small. {idea}That Day's scene makes all of it nothing.{/idea} You will be standing in it too.
old: I am the center of my own world.
new: Before the Throne and its angels, I am small, and that is the right size.
try: In your next sujood, remember the greatness of the One you bow to.

title: Presented before Allah, with nothing hidden.
subtitle: No secret stays secret that Day
then: Ibn Kathir says you will be presented to {idea}the Knower of secrets and private counsels{/idea}, from Whom none of your affairs are hidden. The Prophet ﷺ said people will be shown three times: {trap}twice with arguing and excuses{/trap}, then the records fly into their hands.
now: Your search history. The deleted messages. The thought you never said out loud. {trap}You might have an excuse ready for each.{/trap} {idea}That Day, excuses run out and only the record speaks.{/idea}
old: I can always explain myself later.
new: Nothing is hidden from Allah, so I live now as if my record is open.
try: Delete or stop one thing in your private life you would not want shown that Day.

title: Here, read my record! The joy of the right hand.
subtitle: So happy you want everyone to see
then: Ibn Kathir says, out of {reward}extreme pleasure{/reward}, he says to everyone: take my book and read it. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah will bring a servant close, make him admit his sins, then say: {reward}I concealed these for you in the world, and I forgive you today.{/reward}
now: Remember getting a great report card and showing everyone at home. Now imagine that, but forever. {reward}And not because you never failed.{/reward} {idea}Because Allah covered and forgave.{/idea}
old: Only people with spotless records will be happy that Day.
new: Joy that Day can come from Allah's covering and forgiveness of my faults.
try: Ask Allah tonight: cover my faults in this world and forgive them on that Day.

title: I was certain I would meet my account.
subtitle: The belief that shaped a whole life
then: Ibn Kathir explains he means: {idea}I used to be certain in the worldly life that this Day would definitely come.{/idea} He links it to the verse about those {idea}certain that they will meet their Lord.{/idea}
now: You keep receipts because you know tax season comes. You study because the exam is on the calendar. {idea}The person who expects the account lives differently.{/idea} {reward}That certainty is what he is thankful for.{/reward}
old: I believe in the Day of Judgment, but it does not change my week.
new: Real certainty about meeting my account changes how I live today.
try: Before one decision today, ask: how will this look when I meet my account?

title: So he lives a life he is fully pleased with.
subtitle: Satisfaction that never wears off

row.title: the one who expected the account

then: Ibn Kathir says this life is {reward}pleasant.{/reward} After a life of being certain he would meet his account, the one with the right hand {reward}is now in a life he is fully pleased with.{/reward}
now: The new phone feels great for a week. The promotion for a month. {trap}Then the satisfaction fades and you want the next thing.{/trap} {reward}This verse describes a contentment that does not fade.{/reward}
old: If I get the next thing, I will finally be satisfied.
new: Lasting satisfaction is what Allah promises, not what the next purchase brings.
try: Notice one want today. Instead of buying, say: Allah, give me the life that truly pleases.

title: In a garden raised high.
subtitle: Paradise has levels far above each other
then: Ibn Kathir describes it as {reward}elevated, with pleasant stations and eternal joy.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}Paradise has one hundred levels{/reward}, and between each two is like the distance between earth and sky.
now: People aim for the top floor apartment, the corner office, the penthouse view. {idea}This garden is higher than any of it.{/idea} {reward}And there are levels above levels.{/reward}
old: Just getting in is enough. Why aim higher?
new: Paradise is lofty and has many levels, so it is worth striving to rise.
try: Add one extra good deed today, aiming a little higher than yesterday.

title: Its fruit hangs low, within easy reach.
subtitle: Nothing out of reach anymore
then: Al-Bara' bin 'Azib said the fruit will be {reward}close enough to reach while lying on one's bed.{/reward} More than one early scholar said the same. {idea}Nothing will need straining for.{/idea}
now: You work two jobs for things that always seem one paycheck away. You stretch for promotions that keep moving. {trap}Here, everything is just out of reach.{/trap} {reward}There, it is close.{/reward}
old: Life is always reaching for things I cannot quite get.
new: The struggle of reaching ends in a garden where everything is near.
try: When something feels out of reach today, say: Allah, make Paradise's fruit near for me.

title: Eat and drink in peace for what you sent ahead.
subtitle: The days you lived are now the meal

row.title: deeds and His mercy
sub: not even the Prophet ﷺ without it

then: Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}an invitation of blessing, favor and goodness.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said: work and strive, and know that {idea}none of you enters Paradise by his deeds alone{/idea}, not even me, {reward}unless Allah covers me with His mercy.{/reward}
now: The fast in summer, the night you visited the sick, the money you gave quietly. {idea}They feel like they vanish.{/idea} {reward}They are being sent ahead.{/reward} And Allah's mercy is what makes the meal.
old: My good deeds disappear into nothing.
new: What I do now is sent ahead, and Allah's mercy turns it into a feast.
try: Do one good deed today and think of it as sending a meal ahead for yourself.
